issues.author: weaverbot
issues.body:
Follow-up to #7231 (general chat-SFT launcher).

`experiments/sft/configs/delphi_1e22.py` hand-computes `num_train_steps` as a packed 1-epoch count (`total_tokens / seq_len / weight / batch`), which is error-prone: `ChatLmDatasetFormat` packs several conversations per sequence, so a step count derived from raw row counts over-trains by that packing factor.

`marin.experiment.train.train_lm` already solves this with `num_train_epochs`: it reads `TokenizedCache.num_train_tokens` from a resolved dep at run time and computes `ceil(epochs * tokens / (seq_len * batch))`, which counts packed sequences correctly. The SFT launcher cannot reuse it today because:

1. Its deps are `transform_dataset_step` outputs (canonical OpenAI-messages documents), not tokenized caches — there is no `num_train_tokens` to read at build time; Levanter tokenizes/packs inside the training job via `auto_build_caches`.
2. `marin.experiment.data.tokenized` hardcodes `TextLmDatasetFormat` and cannot emit a chat cache (template + completions-only masking).

Proposal: add chat-format support to the marin tokenize helper so the SFT launcher can tokenize each source into a real chat `TokenizedCache` dep, then adopt the `train_lm` `num_train_epochs` path and drop the hand-computed `num_train_steps`.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Scope: larger than a self-contained fix — analysis only, no PR yet.**

# Research

The launcher this issue targets ([`experiments/sft_launcher/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/7231)) only exists in **still-open PR #7231** (`feuer/sft-launcher`, not merged) — there is nothing to patch on `main`, so any implementation must be sequenced after that PR lands or stacked on its branch. The two gaps the issue names are real, but adopting `num_train_epochs` has a hard blocker.

**Relevant code**
- [`experiment/data.py#L164`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e904cc77ffc6e092c8f26b055f934cd45b1e25d1/lib/marin/src/marin/experiment/data.py#L164) - `tokenized()` hardcodes `TextLmDatasetFormat`
- [`tokenize.py#L179`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e904cc77ffc6e092c8f26b055f934cd45b1e25d1/lib/marin/src/marin/processing/tokenize/tokenize.py#L179) - `TokenizeConfig.format` is already a generic `LmDatasetFormatBase` (plumbing exists below `tokenized()`)
- [`attributes.py#L186`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e904cc77ffc6e092c8f26b055f934cd45b1e25d1/lib/marin/src/marin/processing/tokenize/attributes.py#L186) - attribute schema special-cases `TextLmDatasetFormat` — needs a chat branch
- [`train.py#L146-L150`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e904cc77ffc6e092c8f26b055f934cd45b1e25d1/lib/marin/src/marin/experiment/train.py#L146-L150) - **blocker:** `num_train_epochs` raises for a mixture (`len(datasets) != 1`)
- [`train.py#L170-L172`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/e904cc77ffc6e092c8f26b055f934cd45b1e25d1/lib/marin/src/marin/experiment/train.py#L170-L172) - reads `num_train_tokens` from the single train dataset

# Proposed approach (for human review)

**Blocker first.** The Delphi config is a mixture (magpie 0.9 + `delphi_warmup` 0.1), but `num_train_epochs` is single-dataset only. "One packed epoch over the mixture" is ill-defined — a weighted mixture with `stop_strategy="restart"` has no single epoch boundary. Options:

1. **Per-source epoch, then sum** — tokenize each source to its own chat `TokenizedCache`, resolve `ceil(epochs * tokens_i / (seq_len * batch))` per source at run time, sum for `num_train_steps`. Matches the current hand-computed intent (magpie's packed 1-epoch count) and generalizes; needs a mixture-aware helper, not `train_lm` as-is.
2. **Anchor dataset** — define epochs over the dominant source only. Simpler but silently ignores the warmup token count.

Neither is a drop-in reuse of `train_lm`'s `num_train_epochs`; recommend (1) as a new resolver in the launcher (or a mixture extension to `resolve_num_train_steps`).

**Chat-cache support** (independent, lower-risk): add a `format: LmDatasetFormatBase | None` (or explicit chat params) to `tokenized()` instead of the hardcoded `TextLmDatasetFormat`, thread it into the existing `TokenizeConfig.format`, and add a chat branch to `attributes.py` `_attribute_schema`. Then the launcher swaps its `transform_dataset_step` deps for `tokenized(..., format=chat)` caches that carry `num_train_tokens`.

**Sequencing.** This spans `marin.experiment.data`, `marin.processing.tokenize` (schema), and the launcher — multi-module + design work, and it depends on #7231. It should be a stacked PR on `feuer/sft-launcher` (or a follow-up after merge), not a change against `main`. Please confirm the mixture-epoch semantics (option 1 vs 2) before implementation.

issues.author: weaverbot
issues.body:
## Description

Follow-up from #7233. That PR's TPU eval launcher had to ship a full custom image (`docker/evalchemy-tpu/Dockerfile`) purely to add "extra stuff" — the `marin-community/evalchemy` fork + `lm-eval==0.4.12` + boxed-answer graders + an nltk cache — on top of a known-good base (`ghcr.io/open-thoughts/openthoughts-agent:tpu`, vllm-tpu 0.20.0). @rjpower asked whether Iris could let a user customize a base image *natively* so a full Dockerfile isn't needed for the "just install a few things" case. Custom images stay allowed; this is about the common case.

**How images/deps work today**
- A job's image is `ResourceConfig.image` (`lib/fray/src/fray/types.py:407`), forwarded as `task_image` and pulled/run in `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/runtime/docker.py` (`ensure_image`, then `docker create`). Default is `ghcr.io/marin-community/iris-task:latest` (`lib/iris/config/marin.yaml:48`).
- `remote()` (`lib/marin/src/marin/execution/remote.py:80`) only plumbs `extras` + `env_vars`; it leaves `pip_packages=[]` / `setup_scripts=None`, so Iris always `uv sync`s the marin repo into `/app/.venv` (`setup_scripts.py`, `runtime/env.py:29`), even under a custom image.

**The gap that forced a Dockerfile**
1. `EnvironmentConfig` *does* have `pip_packages` / `setup_scripts` (`lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py:562`) that render `uv pip install …`, but they always target `/app/.venv` — never the image's baked venv. The eval needs packages in the image's `/opt/openthoughts/.venv` (where vllm-tpu lives), so it must invoke that interpreter explicitly and no native install path can reach it.
2. Neither `pip_packages` nor `setup_scripts` is plumbed through `remote()`, and there is no `--pip` / `--requirement` / `--setup-script` CLI flag (only `--extra` / `--sync-package` / `--task-image`).
3. No apt/system-package hook. Native installs also re-run every submit (re-clone + re-download over the open internet each job — a cost driver AGENTS.md flags), vs. a baked, digest-pinned image that does it once.

**Proposals (pick one)**
1. *Declared derived layer (recommended):* add `base_image` + `apt_packages` + `pip_packages` (+ a target-venv selector) + verbatim `run_commands` to `ResourceConfig`/`EnvironmentConfig`; Iris renders a Dockerfile, builds via the existing `DockerImageBuilder`/kaniko path, caches by content-hash(base + deps + commit), and pins the digest. Immutable, one-time cost, no per-run network. Needs a build service + registry-push creds.
2. *Setup-into-target-venv hook (lighter):* plumb `setup_scripts` + `--pip` / `--pip-venv <path>` through `remote()` and the CLI, and let `docker.py` activate a user-named venv instead of hardcoding `/app/.venv`. Zero build infra, but re-runs each job and gives no apt layer or immutable pin.

### Definition of Done

- Decide layer-build (1) vs. setup-hook (2).
- A user can add pip (and ideally apt) deps to a chosen base image + target venv from `ResourceConfig`/`remote()` without authoring a Dockerfile.
- The #7233 evalchemy case is expressible natively, or is documented as a legitimate custom-image case if it stays out of scope.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Read issue + `#7233` context
- [x] Verify current image/deps/venv plumbing (fray → iris → docker/k8s)
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no overlapping PR/issue)
- [x] Decide proposal (1) build vs (2) setup-hook and post recommendation

Design decision → no PR; analysis for a human below.

# Research

Most of proposal **(2)** already exists: `setup_scripts` + `pip_packages` are fully plumbed from `create_environment` through iris to *both* the Docker and k8s runtimes, and setup scripts run verbatim as arbitrary bash with the task's `IRIS_*` env available. Three concrete gaps block the #7233 evalchemy case from being native:

1. **Single fixed venv target.** `VENV_PATH` is hardcoded to `/app/.venv` and exported as `IRIS_VENV`; the default uv-sync script, iris runtime-deps script, and the run-phase activation all key off it. There is no selector to install into / activate the image's baked venv (`/opt/openthoughts/.venv`).
2. **`remote()` drops the hooks.** It only forwards `extras` + `env_vars`, leaving `pip_packages=[]` / `setup_scripts=None`, so every submit re-runs the default `uv sync` of the marin repo — even under a custom image.
3. **No CLI flag and no apt layer.** Runners expose `--extra` / `--task-image` but no `--pip` / `--setup-script`; system packages have no hook at all.

**Relevant code**
- [`remote.py#L80-L84`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/execution/remote.py#L80-L84) — `remote()` passes only extras/env_vars
- [`fray/types.py#L560-L610`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/fray/src/fray/types.py#L560-L610) — `EnvironmentConfig`/`create_environment` already carry `pip_packages`+`setup_scripts`
- [`iris/cluster/types.py#L735-L780`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py#L735-L780) — renders setup scripts; `None` ⇒ default uv-sync, `[]` ⇒ image as-is
- [`setup_scripts.py#L57-L207`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/setup_scripts.py#L57-L207) — `default_setup_script` / `iris_runtime_setup_script`, all writing `$IRIS_VENV`
- [`runtime/env.py#L29-L30`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/runtime/env.py#L29-L30) — `VENV_PATH = "/app/.venv"` (the fixed target); activation at [`docker.py#L537`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/runtime/docker.py#L537) / [`k8s/tasks.py#L450`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/backends/k8s/tasks.py#L450)

# Proposed approach

**Recommend (2), the setup-into-target-venv hook — not (1).** ~80% of it is already built and merged; the delta is small and needs zero build/registry infra. Reserve custom Dockerfiles (and a future (1)) for the immutable-pin / apt-heavy case. Scope:

- **Target-venv selector.** Generalize the hardcoded `VENV_PATH`: let a job name the venv the default sync/pip installs into and that the run phase activates (default stays `/app/.venv`). This is the one change that makes "install into the image's baked venv" native; `IRIS_VENV` is already an env var, so `docker.py`/`k8s/tasks.py`/`setup_scripts.py` only need to stop assuming a single constant.
- **Plumb `pip_packages` + `setup_scripts` through `remote()`** (and `RemoteCallable`) into `create_environment` — the fields already exist downstream, `remote()` just needs to forward them.
- **CLI `--pip` / `--setup-script`** on the runner alongside `--extra` / `--task-image`.

**apt / system packages: out of scope for (2), document as the custom-image case.** Runtime `apt-get` re-runs and re-downloads over the open internet every submit — exactly the cost AGENTS.md flags. A one-time baked layer is the right tool, which is proposal (1)'s territory.

**On (1):** worth it only if per-run network cost (the #7233 fork-clone + lm-eval + nltk re-download every job) becomes a recurring pain. It needs a build service, registry-push creds, and content-hash caching — real infra for a case a digest-pinned custom image already covers today. Defer until (2) is in use and the re-download cost is measured.

**Net for #7233:** the pip-into-baked-venv piece becomes native via the selector + `remote()` plumbing; the nltk-cache/apt/immutable-pin pieces remain a legitimate custom-image case. Flagging @rjpower for a call on selector-only (2) vs. investing in the (1) build path.

issues.author: Helw150
issues.body:
🤖 Picks up **item 3 (arbitrary tool use)** of #7090 — the easy, base-model end of it.

## Dataset

https://huggingface.co/datasets/marin-community/mcp-atlas-easy

**MCP-Atlas-Easy** is a 220-row single-tool-call benchmark for *pretrained (base) models*, derived from [ScaleAI/MCP-Atlas](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ScaleAI/mcp-atlas) (36 real MCP servers, 220 tools, CC-BY-4.0). MCP-Atlas evaluates instruction-tuned agents on multi-step orchestration (3–6 calls per task); this strips the same skill down to its simplest form: **one tool spec, one trivially unambiguous request, one correct tool call, then stop.**

## Format

One row per unique tool. Each row carries structured fields (`tool`, `server`, `description`, `input_schema`, `scenario`, `target_call`) plus ready-to-use `prompt`/`completion` strings:

```
The following is a demonstration of correct tool use. Given a tool
specification and a user request, the assistant responds with a single
JSON tool call.

Tool specification:
{
  "name": "whois_whois_domain",
  "description": "Look up WHOIS registration information for a domain name.",
  "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"domain": {...}}, "required": ["domain"]}
}

User request: Look up WHOIS information for the domain openai.com.

Tool call: {"name": "whois_whois_domain", "arguments": {"domain": "openai.com"}}<|endoftext|>
```

The target completion is the JSON call followed by `<|endoftext|>` (swap for the tokenizer's real EOS when building eval inputs), so it works as a completion-style eval with no chat template and scores two things: **call correctness** (parse the JSON, match against `target_call` / validate against `input_schema`) and **clean stopping** (does the model emit EOS or degenerate into continuation).

## Construction

1. Extracted all 220 unique tool names from MCP-Atlas `ENABLED_TOOLS`, plus per-tool evidence: declared required/optional params (41 tools) and real invocation arguments mined from the `TRAJECTORY` fields (106 tools).
2. Claude Sonnet generated a grounded spec (description + JSON Schema) and one deliberately easy scenario + correct call per tool.
3. Programmatic validation: every target call satisfies its own schema (required args present, no undeclared args); all 220 tools covered exactly once.

## Caveats

- **103/220 schemas are inferred.** Those tools are never called in the public MCP-Atlas trajectories and have no declared params, so schemas were inferred from tool names and known server behavior (e.g. `f1-mcp-server_*`, `anili_*`, most `notion_API-*`). Rows are always internally consistent — the target call matches the spec shown in the prompt — but inferred schemas may not match the real servers' wire formats. Treat as a formatting/grounding eval, not a live-server integration test.
- Scenarios and calls are synthetic (Claude Sonnet), not human-authored.

## Open follow-ups toward the full item 3

- These are real, public MCP servers, so the "unlikely to appear in the pretraining corpus" criterion is only partially met. A follow-up could mutate tool names/schemas (or synthesize novel tools) to guarantee unseen-ness.
- Harder variants: multiple tools in context (selection, not just invocation), optional-arg scenarios, distractor tools, and multi-step composition — bridging back toward full MCP-Atlas difficulty.

comments.author: claude[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 **Plan:**
- [x] Actionability check — issue is actionable but larger than a self-contained bug fix
- [x] Research eval framework (registry, inline HF tasks, generation scoring)
- [x] Duplicate-work preflight (no open PR/issue for this)
- [x] Post analysis + proposed approach (below) — **no PR**, awaiting human review

Scope: new eval + custom scoring (>100 lines, design decisions on generation vs loglikelihood and how to register a tool-call metric). Per the fix-issue policy for features/design work, posting analysis instead of a PR.

# Research

Marin's lm-eval path already supports **fully-inline HF-dataset tasks**: `EvalTaskConfig.task_kwargs` is spread into Levanter's `TaskConfig`, so `dataset_path`, `output_type="generation"`, `metric_list`, and `additional_stop_strings` can be passed without registering a YAML. The gap for MCP-Atlas-Easy is **scoring**: lm-eval has no built-in metric that (a) extracts+parses the JSON tool call, (b) validates it against `input_schema` / matches `target_call`, or (c) measures clean stopping (EOS vs. degenerate continuation). That scorer has to be added.

**Relevant code**
- [`evaluation_config.py#L104-L119`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evaluation_config.py#L104-L119) — `task_kwargs` spread into `TaskConfig` (inline HF tasks)
- [`eval_harness.py#L1046-L1062`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval_harness.py#L1046-L1062) — inline fields: `dataset_path`, `output_type`, `metric_list`, `additional_stop_strings`
- [`task_configs.py#L86`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/task_configs.py#L86) — existing 0-shot generation task (`ifeval`) to mirror
- [`run.py#L31-L37`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/run.py#L31) — `EVALUATORS` registry
- [`evals.py#L220`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/evals/evals.py#L220) — `default_base_eval` entry point where a base-model tool-use task would be surfaced

# Proposed Approach

The dataset already ships `prompt`/`completion` plus structured `target_call`/`input_schema`, so no dataset work is needed. Two viable designs:

**Option A — inline generation task + custom lm-eval metric (recommended).**
Define `mcp_atlas_easy` as an inline `TaskConfig`: `output_type="generation"`, `doc_to_text=` the `prompt` field, `additional_stop_strings=["<|endoftext|>"]` (plus the real EOS at build time). Add a small registered scorer that computes two metrics per row:
- `tool_call_match` — `json.loads` the first JSON object in the completion; require `name == target_call.name` and arguments satisfying `input_schema` (required present, no undeclared) and matching `target_call.arguments`.
- `clean_stop` — model emitted EOS/stop before the generation cap (no runaway continuation).

Wire it as an `EvalTaskConfig(name="mcp_atlas_easy", num_fewshot=0, task_kwargs={...})` in `task_configs.py`, exposed via a `TOOL_USE_TASKS` tuple. Est. ~150–250 lines incl. the scorer + one behavior test (a handful of hand-written completions: exact match, wrong tool, schema-violating args, non-JSON, missing-EOS — asserting each metric flips correctly).

**Option B — standalone `ToolUseEvaluator` in `EVALUATORS`.** More control (drive vLLM directly, richer per-row diagnostics) but duplicates generation plumbing lm-eval already provides. Heavier; prefer only if Option A's metric registration proves awkward inside Levanter's harness.

**Open questions for a human before implementation:**
1. Base-model generation backend — run under the **Levanter** lm-eval path (`levanter_lm_evaluation_harness`) or the **vLLM** one (`lm_evaluation_harness`)? Affects where the custom metric registers and how EOS is detected.
2. Scoring strictness — exact `arguments` match vs. schema-valid-and-required-args-present (the 103/220 inferred-schema rows argue for the looser variant as the headline metric, with exact-match reported separately).
3. Report `tool_call_match` and `clean_stop` as two separate metrics, or a combined "correct call AND clean stop"?

Recommend Option A pending answers to (1)–(3).

comments.author: penfever
comments.body:
🤖 Approximate post-training cost, as the pipeline runs today.

## The answer

Pipeline: **RL 10 experts → MOPD into the student** (Nemotron path). Costed in **HW FLOPs** (= `model_FLOPs / MFU` = device-FLOP-seconds — the pretraining plan's currency, so the low-MFU cost of RL/OPD is counted, not hidden; agentic RL currently runs at **~1% aggregate MFU** vs ~15% for pretraining). The RL leg (the dominant cost) runs on **experts, which are ≥ the hero**, so per-run cost scales with the expert's **hosting footprint** (∝ total params).

| experts (≥ hero) | per-run HW-FLOPs | K=10 create → saturate | vs hero **10T** (1.11e24) | vs hero **2T cut** (2.43e23) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **= hero** (67B-A2B) | ~1.4×10²² | ~2.8×10²³ → 5.6×10²³ | 0.25 → 0.5× | 1.2 → **2.3×** |
| **big** (120B-A20B) | ~2.4×10²² | ~4.8×10²³ → 9.6×10²³ | 0.43 → 0.86× | 2.0 → **3.9×** |

*(create = 1 run/expert; saturate ≈ 2 runs (small-hero fast convergence); full 4-run saturate ≈ 2× these. A **~5× env speedup** divides everything by 5. Per-run scales an 8B-measured anchor (8×10²¹) by the expert's hosting footprint: 67B ≈ 1.75×, 120B ≈ 3×.)*

**Headline: because experts ≥ hero, post-training a *small* 67B-A2B hero costs ~0.25–0.9× its 10T pretraining — or ~1.2–3.9× its cheap 2T-cut pretraining.** Against the *120B big run* it's still only ~5–20%. A **~5× environment speedup** drops all of this ~5× (small hero + =-hero experts → ~0.05–0.1× the 10T cut).

On the literal token question: we probably only need **~10⁹–10¹⁰ training tokens, <0.5% of a 10T pretrain** — but that's misleading, because each post-training token costs **~700× the HW FLOPs of a pretraining token** (≈10× lower MFU × ~70× more passes/token: multi-sample rollout + ref/teacher forwards + long-context re-prefill), so **0.02% of the tokens becomes ~14% of the HW-FLOP budget**. Budget in HW FLOPs, not tokens.

### Cost formula

**`HW-FLOPs_to_saturate = gap × (tokens/nat) × bpp × N_active × (peak/BW) / MBU`** — linear in **N_active**, **independent of n_GPU** (parallelism buys wall-clock, not cost; the memory-bound analog of "6ND is GPU-count-invariant"). Two size taxes: **env-bound today → cost ∝ total params** (idle rollout GPUs billed by count = footprint); **decode-bound after the env fix → cost ∝ active params**.

## The two RL-cost regimes (the evidence)

**Agentic RL (environment-bound).** Measured on an 8B run (`56GPU_qwen3_8b.yaml`, 48 engines TP=1 + 8 policy/ref): step wall ~1,500–2,500 s, ~80 steps → **~40 h/run ≈ 2.3k GPU-h**. The wall is **79–94% `wait_for_generation_buffer`, ~4–18% training, ~1% decode** — engines are request-starved, not compute-bound (throughput **271–568 tok/s** vs a **~1000 tok/s** ceiling, waiting≈0, KV 20–65%; the recipe over-provisions decode 3× on purpose so the trainer never waits on gen). The constraint is the environment (sandbox/tool/verifier), **not buyable with FLOPs** — the lever is a faster container backend (vs Daytona) and RL-loop hardening (Ray/Harbor).

**Non-agentic RL (decode-bound).** From #6279 (Delphi MATH500): pass@1 0.45 → pass@128 (latent) 0.796 = **1.56-nat gap**; `rlvr7500` closed **22%** of it at **≈8.7×10⁸ rollout-tok/nat**. Decode-bandwidth-bound, so `wall = gap × cost_per_nat / (HBM_BW × MBU × #GPU)`; per capability axis this is ~10⁴–10⁵ GPU-h at the hero N_active (MBU 0.1–0.4), ×#axes.

**RL efficiency → "~4 runs to saturate".** Each run closes **~20–25% of the available pass@k headroom** in both regimes (#6279 math 22% of pass@128; the swesmith agentic run 25% of pass@8), so ~4 runs/expert to saturate (optimistic-linear — diminishing returns push higher).

**Why MOPD is load-bearing.** On the exact RL task (`DCAgent/exp_rpt_pymethods2test-large`), the **122B teacher scores reward 0.513 — above the 8B student's pass@8 ceiling of 0.327.** RL only converts latent pass@k into pass@1, so it **cannot reach the teacher**; the student→teacher gap (**1.53 nats, ~2× the pass@8 gap**) must be closed by **distillation, not RL**. (The 4,668 teacher traces are a free SFT-distillation seed.)

---

Biggest open assumptions: **expert size** (≥ hero — sets the whole RL bill), **runs-to-saturate** (~2 for a small hero vs 4), **MFU/MBU**, and the H100 peak used for HW-FLOP conversion. Sources: RL scaling #6279; agentic runs `experiments/complete/ablation_exploration_in_rl` (`swesmith-…-75-8B`, trained 2026-06-18); teacher reference `completed_datasets_summary.csv`; pretraining HW FLOPs from the planning sheet.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
🤖
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This experiment is building a DeepEP-free single-node EP8 Grug MoE path using Pallas Mosaic MGPU remote refs, with fused routed-token dispatch into expert-major tiles followed by W13/SiLU expert compute on 8xH100. The first handoff established the spec, baselines, and implementation path; the latest validation added a prepacked dispatch oracle, a shard-local remote-ref validation primitive, and a local fused W13/SiLU Pallas kernel. H100x8 smoke runs now show exact dispatch payload/metadata parity for top-k 1 and top-k 4, with W13/SiLU max error 2 in bf16, so the immediate remaining work is tiled/staged dispatch plus backward/custom-VJP coverage before any training integration claim.

### Helpful links
- Spec branch handoff: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6597#issuecomment-4783570735
- Scope assessment and relevant MoE backends: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6597#issuecomment-4783575997
- Milestones 1 and 2 H100 validation update: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/6597#issuecomment-4783991292
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Scope

Target hardware: one 8xH100 NVLink island first; future NVL72/GB200 is the medium-term motivation.

Target backend: a new experimental Grug MoE backend, likely mosaic_mgpu, wired next to ring/ragged_all_to_all under lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe. Do not use DeepEP, NCCL EP, FFI transport, NIC, RDMA, or NVSHMEM for this path.

Primary spec branch: codex/pallas-mosaic-mgpu-moe-spec

Spec path on branch: .agents/projects/pallas_mosaic_mgpu_moe_spec.md

Research logbook path: .agents/logbooks/pallas-mosaic-mgpu-moe.md

## Hypothesis or Goal

A Pallas Mosaic MGPU kernel can route token blocks directly into destination expert-major tiles and consume them with W13/SiLU, avoiding the wrapper/permutation/opaque-FFI costs that made DeepEP hard to profile and unreliable.

The first validation slice is remote dispatch layout correctness. The first product milestone is fused dispatch + W13/SiLU for top-k 4 on EP8. The training milestone requires a custom VJP/backward path and fwd+bwd+SGD profile.

## Current Baselines

- DeepEP EP16/N2 B64 save_moe May387 reached about 17 MFU, but DeepEP has repeatedly hit recv-counter timeouts.
- EP8/B16 readable profiles May363/May378 showed MoE around 37-40% of step time.
- Ring/ragged A2A remain more debuggable than DeepEP, but ragged_all_to_all was slower than ring in the tested shape.
- SonicMoE is included as a local expert compute/layout reference, not an EP transport reference.

## Required Deliverables

- Readable JAX reference for routing/layout and forward math.
- Pallas Mosaic MGPU remote dispatch validation slice.
- Fused dispatch + W13/SiLU kernel for top-k 4.
- W_down and combine path sufficient for full forward parity.
- Custom VJP plan and small-shape gradient parity before training claims.
- Performance harness reporting prepack, dispatch, W13, SiLU, W2, combine, backward W13/SiLU, and backward transport.
- Comparison against ring and ragged_all_to_all on the same single-node shape.

## Decision Log

- 2026-06-23: Start with 8xH100 single-node EP8. Keep DeepEP out of this path; it is a baseline only.
- 2026-06-23: Product target is fused dispatch + W13/SiLU. Dispatch-only exists only as a validation slice.
- 2026-06-23: Include backward/custom VJP in the plan before training integration.

## Negative Results Index

- DeepEP May391 fixed-metadata profile attempt failed on step 1 with internode recv-counter timeouts before producing a useful profile.
- Prior DeepEP targeted offload variants also hit recv-counter timeouts or underperformed.

## Completion Criteria

- EP8 single-node 8xH100 fused dispatch + W13/SiLU works for top-k 4.
- Values match a JAX reference and one existing backend on small and realistic shapes.
- A custom VJP exists and passes small-shape gradient parity, even if the first backward implementation is reference/JAX rather than Mosaic.
- A fwd+bwd+SGD profile runs with model_axis=1 and phase-attributed named scopes.
- The report compares against ring and ragged_all_to_all on the same shape.

🤖 **Scope assessment: research experiment, not an automated-PR task.**

This is an `experiment` tracker for greenfield GPU-kernel work, not a self-contained bug fix. It is out of scope for an automated PR for three reasons:

- **Multi-module, far beyond 100 LOC.** Deliverables include a new `mosaic_mgpu` MoE backend (JAX reference, remote-dispatch validation slice, fused dispatch + W13/SiLU kernel, W_down/combine, custom VJP, perf harness). No `mgpu`/`mosaic` code exists yet under `lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/` — `grep -rilE 'mgpu|mosaic'` returns nothing.
- **Hardware-gated.** Completion criteria require validation on a single-node 8×H100 NVLink island (EP8, top-k 4) with a fwd+bwd+SGD profile. None of this is verifiable in CI.
- **Custom-VJP / numerical-parity design work** that needs human review before training integration, per the issue's own Decision Log.

**Existing artifacts** (already authored — do not duplicate):
- Spec branch `codex/pallas-mosaic-mgpu-moe-spec` carries `.agents/projects/pallas_mosaic_mgpu_moe_spec.md` and `.agents/logbooks/pallas-mosaic-mgpu-moe.md` (neither is on `main`).

**Relevant code** — the EP backends the new path sits beside and must match for parity:
- [`grug/_moe/ep_ring.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ring.py) — ring A2A baseline (most debuggable per baselines).
- [`grug/_moe/ep_ragged_all_to_all.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_ragged_all_to_all.py) — ragged A2A comparison target.
- [`grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/ep_deepep.py) — DeepEP baseline (kept out of new path; baseline only).

**Recommended path:** drive this from the spec branch with a human owner, landing the deliverables incrementally (JAX reference → dispatch validation slice → fused W13/SiLU → backward/VJP → perf harness). The `add-pallas-kernel` and `change-grug` skills cover the kernel and Grug-variant mechanics. comments.body:
🤖 MoE MGPU CoreWeave scale probe update (2026-06-29):

What works now:
- Single-node L2 pallas_mgpu smoke remains the known good baseline (~20% MFU from `/dlwh/grug-moe-pallas-mgpu-20step-smoke-2d87348e7`).

What fails:
- Multi-node without the NVSHMEM XLA flag fails to load NVSHMEM.
- Multi-node with the flag but normal 8-GPU-per-process Iris topology fails with `NVSHMEM API is only supported with one device per process`.
- Multi-node with one process per GPU gets past both of those, creates the intended task topology (`r2-t16x1` on N2; N4 also got to this stage), then fails during NVSHMEM UID bootstrap. The failure is repeated `socketStartConnect: exceeded timeouts (3)` followed by `Bootstrap plugin init failed for 'nvshmem_bootstrap_uid.so.3'`.\n\nMost recent committed N2 probe:\n- Parent: `/dlwh/grug-moe-pallas-mgpu-target-20step-r2-onegpu2-20260629-223542`\n- Child created 16 one-GPU tasks and ran ~7 minutes before the bootstrap failure; I stopped it after failure_count=1 to avoid retry churn.\n\nConclusion: N1 works; multi-node Pallas MGPU is currently blocked below the model/CE layer on NVSHMEM bootstrap under Iris one-process-per-GPU. Next useful work is Iris/CoreWeave NVSHMEM bootstrap/process-per-device support, not another 4/8/16/32 scale sweep until that is fixed.

High-level approach: the current source-push lane is staged around one expert-MLP custom VJP boundary over `x`, `route_assignments`, `route_weights`, `w13`, and `w2`. Forward builds the source-push plan, pushes routed `x` into expert-major rows, runs W13, and saves W13 preactivation `H` (`[gate, up]`) in the expert-major/flat H-row layout. comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Update: source-push MoE MLP kernel pseudocode

Below is pseudocode in the SonicMoE “Algorithm N / parallel-for / grouped-GEMM” style, adapted to the current EP source-push design. SonicMoE frames MoE around gathered expert rows, varlen-M grouped GEMM for forward/activation grads, and varlen-K grouped GEMM for weight grads; our main difference is that expert rows are produced by MGPU source-push routing instead of local gather. Reference: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.14080.

Notation:

```text
R             = ep_size / number of ranks
E_l           = local experts per rank
C             = expert capacity per local expert
D             = hidden dim
I             = intermediate dim
K             = top-k routes per token
X_r           = source-rank input tokens [T, D]
W13_r,e       = local expert up/gate weight [D, 2I]
W2_r,e        = local expert down weight [I, D]
Plan          = compact source-push routing metadata
H_r,e,c       = W13 preactivation [E_l, C, 2I]
A_r,e,c       = silu(gate(H)) * up(H), usually not saved
```

Algorithm 1: Build SourcePushPlan

```text
Input:
  assignments[r, t, k]     // global expert ids
  route_weights[r, t, k]
  capacity_factor

Output:
  Plan:
    dst_rank[r,t,k]
    local_expert[r,t,k]
    expert_row[r,t,k]
    source_rank_by_expert[dst,e,c]
    token_id_by_expert[dst,e,c]
    route_weight_by_expert[dst,e,c]
    valid_by_expert[dst,e,c]
    return metadata for y/dx combine

for each source rank r in parallel:
  for each token t and route k:
    g = assignments[r,t,k]
    dst = owner_rank(g)
    e = local_expert_id(g)
    c = atomic_or_prefix_slot(dst,e)

    Plan.dst_rank[r,t,k] = dst
    Plan.local_expert[r,t,k] = e
    Plan.expert_row[r,t,k] = c
    Plan.source_rank_by_expert[dst,e,c] = r
    Plan.token_id_by_expert[dst,e,c] = t
    Plan.route_weight_by_expert[dst,e,c] = route_weights[r,t,k]
    Plan.valid_by_expert[dst,e,c] = true
```

Algorithm 2: Forward W13 Source-Push Inbox

```text
Input:
  X_r [T,D] on each source rank
  W13_dst,e [D,2I] on each destination rank
  Plan

Output:
  H_dst,e,c [E_l,C,2I]   // saved forward residual

// source-side producer CTAs
for each source rank src in parallel:
  for each destination rank dst:
    for each source-push queue entry q assigned to (src,dst):
      rows = Plan routes from src to dst in this expert group / row block
      copy X_src[token_id(rows), :] into dst inbox slot
      release inbox semaphore(slot)

// destination-side consumer / W13 CTAs
for each destination rank dst in parallel:
  for each local expert group EG:
    for each ready inbox entry from any source src:
      wait inbox semaphore(slot)

      for each expert e in EG:
        for each output-N tile n of W13:
          acc_gate = 0
          acc_up = 0

          for k_tile over D:
            load inbox X tile [M, K] into SMEM
            load W13_gate[e, K, N] into SMEM
            load W13_up[e, K, N] into SMEM
            WGMMA acc_gate += X @ W13_gate
            WGMMA acc_up   += X @ W13_up

          store acc_gate, acc_up to
            H_dst,e,row_block,n
```

Key property: the stable residual is `H`, not packed `X`, not post-SwiGLU `A`.

Algorithm 3: Forward W2 From H + Return/Combine

```text
Input:
  H_dst,e,c [E_l,C,2I]
  W2_dst,e [I,D]
  route_weight_by_expert[dst,e,c]
  return metadata from Plan

Output:
  Y_src [T,D]

for each destination rank dst in parallel:
  for each local expert e:
    for each row block c_block:
      gate, up = split(H[e,c_block,:])
      A = silu(gate) * up
      A_weighted = route_weight_by_expert[e,c_block] * A

      for each output-D tile n:
        acc = 0
        for k_tile over I:
          load A_weighted[M,K] into SMEM
          load W2[e,K,N] into SMEM
          WGMMA acc += A_weighted @ W2

        send or stage partial Y rows back to source rank

for each source rank src in parallel:
  for each returned route contribution:
    t = token_id
    Y_src[t,:] += returned_partial
```

Algorithm 4: Full Forward MLP Boundary

```text
Input:
  X, assignments, route_weights, W13, W2

Output:
  Y
  residual = (Plan, H_expert_major, route_weight_by_expert, static config)

Plan = BuildSourcePushPlan(assignments, route_weights)
H = SourcePushW13H(X, W13, Plan)
Y = SourcePushW2FromHReturnCombine(H, W2, Plan)

save_for_backward(Plan, H, route_weight_by_expert, config)
return Y
```

Algorithm 5: Backward dy Route

```text
Input:
  dY_src [T,D]
  Plan

Output:
  dY_expert_dst,e,c [E_l,C,D]

for each source rank src in parallel:
  for each token t and route k:
    dst = Plan.dst_rank[src,t,k]
    e   = Plan.local_expert[src,t,k]
    c   = Plan.expert_row[src,t,k]

    push dY_src[t,:] to dst expert row (e,c)

for each destination rank dst in parallel:
  receive dY rows into compact expert-major layout
```

Algorithm 6: W2 Backward

```text
Input:
  dY_expert[e,c,D]
  H[e,c,2I]
  W2[e,I,D]
  route_weight_by_expert[e,c]

Output:
  dA_weighted[e,c,I]
  dW2[e,I,D]
  d_route_weight[e,c] later

for each destination rank dst in parallel:
  for each local expert e:
    // recompute activation from saved H
    gate, up = split(H[e,:,:])
    A = silu(gate) * up
    A_weighted = route_weight_by_expert[e,:] * A

    // activation gradient: varlen-M grouped GEMM
    for row block c and I tile i:
      acc = 0
      for d_tile over D:
        load dY[c,d_tile]
        load W2[e,i,d_tile]
        WGMMA acc += dY @ W2^T
      store dA_weighted[c,i] = acc

    // weight gradient: varlen-K grouped GEMM
    for I tile i and D tile d:
      acc = 0
      for c_block over expert rows:
        load A_weighted[c_block,i]
        load dY[c_block,d]
        WGMMA acc += A_weighted^T @ dY
      store dW2[e,i,d] = acc
```

Algorithm 7: Route-Weight Grad + SwiGLU Backward

```text
Input:
  dA_weighted[e,c,I]
  H[e,c,2I]
  route_weight_by_expert[e,c]

Output:
  dH[e,c,2I]
  d_route_weight[e,c]

for each destination rank dst in parallel:
  for each expert e and row c:
    gate, up = split(H[e,c,:])
    A = silu(gate) * up

    d_route_weight[e,c] = dot(dA_weighted[e,c,:], A)

    dA = route_weight_by_expert[e,c] * dA_weighted[e,c,:]

    d_up = dA * silu(gate)
    d_gate = dA * up * d_silu(gate)

    dH[e,c,:] = concat(d_gate, d_up)
```

Algorithm 8: Rematerialize X Expert-Major

```text
Input:
  X_src [T,D]
  Plan

Output:
  X_expert_dst,e,c [E_l,C,D]

for each source rank src in parallel:
  for each route row assigned by Plan:
    dst = Plan.dst_rank
    e   = Plan.local_expert
    c   = Plan.expert_row
    push X_src[token_id,:] to dst expert row (e,c)

for each destination rank dst:
  receive into X_expert[e,c,:]
```

This is the simple staged version. The experimental W13 source-gather path tries to avoid materializing this full `X_expert_major` by gathering source rows per WGMMA tile.

Algorithm 9: W13 Backward, Staged Compact Version

```text
Input:
  X_expert[e,c,D]
  dH[e,c,2I]
  W13[e,D,2I]

Output:
  dW13[e,D,2I]
  dX_expert[e,c,D]

for each destination rank dst in parallel:
  for each local expert e:
    // dx expert-major: varlen-M grouped GEMM
    for row block c and D tile d:
      acc = 0
      for h_tile over 2I:
        load dH[c,h_tile]
        load W13[e,d,h_tile]
        WGMMA acc += dH @ W13^T
      store dX_expert[c,d] = acc

    // dW13: varlen-K grouped GEMM
    for D tile d and H tile h:
      acc = 0
      for row block c:
        load X_expert[c,d]
        load dH[c,h]
        WGMMA acc += X_expert^T @ dH
      store dW13[e,d,h] = acc
```

Algorithm 10: W13 Backward, Experimental Source-Gather dW13

```text
Input:
  source-major X_src [R,T,D]
  dH_dst,e,c [E_l,C,2I]
  source_rank_by_expert[e,c]
  token_id_by_expert[e,c]
  valid_by_expert[e,c]

Output:
  dW13[e,D,2I]

for each destination rank dst in parallel:
  for each local expert e:
    for D tile d and H tile h:
      acc = 0

      for row block c_block:
        // current lowering-friendly form
        X_tile = zeros[M,D_tile]

        for static source rank src in 0..R-1:
          tokens = token_id_by_expert[e,c_block]
          mask = valid_by_expert[e,c_block]
                 && source_rank_by_expert[e,c_block] == src

          // remote source gather
          X_src_tile = remote_load(X_src[src, tokens, d_tile])
          X_tile += where(mask, X_src_tile, 0)

        dH_tile = load dH[e,c_block,h_tile]

        WGMMA acc += X_tile^T @ dH_tile

      store dW13[e,d,h] = acc
```

This is the current experimental direction. It avoids full `X_expert_major` GMEM staging, but may overfetch unless source-sorted/packed by source rank.

Algorithm 11: dx Return/Combine

```text
Input:
  dX_expert_dst,e,c [E_l,C,D]
  Plan return metadata

Output:
  dX_src [T,D]

for each destination rank dst in parallel:
  for each expert row (e,c):
    src = source_rank_by_expert[e,c]
    t   = token_id_by_expert[e,c]
    push dX_expert[e,c,:] back to source rank src

for each source rank src in parallel:
  initialize dX_src = 0
  for each returned route contribution:
    dX_src[token_id,:] += dX_route
```

Algorithm 12: Full Custom VJP Backward

```text
Input:
  dY_src
  saved residual: Plan, H, route_weight_by_expert, config
  original params: W13, W2
  original X for rematerialization

Output:
  dX, dW13, dW2, d_route_weights

dY_expert = RouteDyToExpertMajor(dY_src, Plan)

dA_weighted, dW2 = W2Backward(dY_expert, H, W2, route_weight_by_expert)

dH, d_route_weight_by_expert =
  RouteWeightGradAndSwiGLUBackward(dA_weighted, H, route_weight_by_expert)

X_expert = RematerializeXExpertMajor(X, Plan)
dX_expert, dW13 = W13Backward(X_expert, dH, W13)

dX = ReturnCombineDx(dX_expert, Plan)

d_route_weights = scatter_expert_major_to_original_route_order(
  d_route_weight_by_expert, Plan
)

return dX, dW13, dW2, d_route_weights
```

The design target is: forward saves `H_expert_major`; backward recomputes `A`, routes `dy`, computes W2 grads, derives `dH`, rematerializes only what W13 backward needs, then returns `dx`.

comments.author: dlwh
comments.body:
🤖 Handoff: semantic queue model and fused MoE stage boundaries

At the target shape, the MoE MLP is mostly a problem of moving token-route data between expert-parallel ranks without letting communication serialize the tensorcore work.

Conceptually the MLP is:

```text
forward:
  permute -> W13 -> activation -> W2 -> combine

backward:
  dcombine -> dW2_h / dW2_w -> dactivation -> dW13_x / dW13_w -> dpermute
```

Where:

- `permute`, `combine`, `dcombine`, and `dpermute` are communication-heavy.
- `W13`, `W2`, `dW2_*`, and `dW13_*` are tensorcore-heavy.
- The central optimization goal is to overlap communication-heavy passes with adjacent GEMM work, instead of materializing all routed tensors and then computing.

### Forward fused stages

`permute_w13`

Inputs:

```text
x[src, token, hidden]
routing[token, k] -> global expert / dst rank / local expert / weight
w13[dst, local_expert, hidden, 2 * intermediate]
```

Output:

```text
h_expert[dst, local_expert, expert_row, intermediate]
```

Intent: send routed token tiles from source ranks to destination ranks that own the experts, then compute W13 on the destination as data arrives. This replaces:

```text
all_to_all full x -> materialized recv_x -> W13
```

with:

```text
send token tile to owning expert rank
destination computes W13/SiLU as the tile becomes available
store h in expert-major layout
```

Pseudocode:

```python
for work in permute_w13_queue:
    Permute1(src, dst, entry):
        send x[src, token_ids[src,dst,entry], :] to dst slot/queue

    Compute1(dst, src, entry, expert_group, m_tile, n_tile):
        x_tile = read received source-token tile
        z_tile = x_tile @ w13[dst, expert, :, n_tile]
        h_tile = silu(z_gate) * z_up
        h_expert[dst, expert, rows, :] = h_tile
```

`w2_return`

Inputs:

```text
h_expert[dst, local_expert, expert_row, intermediate]
w2[dst, local_expert, intermediate, hidden]
return metadata: expert_row -> source rank, return queue entry, queue row
```

Output:

```text
return_y[src, dst_ord, entry, row, hidden]
```

Intent: compute W2 on the expert-owning rank, then write each route result directly into the source rank’s return queue. This should remove the old dense replicated path:

```text
route_y_expert -> partial_y[src, token, hidden] -> psum(partial_y)
```

and replace it with:

```text
route_y_expert -> source-visible return_y queue
```

Pseudocode:

```python
for work in w2_return_queue:
    Compute2(dst, expert, expert_rows, h_tile):
        y_tile = h_expert[dst, expert, expert_rows, :] @ w2[dst, expert, :, h_tile]

    Return2(dst, src, entry, queue_rows, h_tile):
        write y_tile to return_y[src, dst_ord, entry, queue_rows, h_tile]
```

`combine`

Inputs:

```text
return_y[src, dst_ord, entry, row, hidden]
queue_dst_ord[src, token, k]
queue_entry[src, token, k]
queue_row[src, token, k]
route_weight[src, token, k]
```

Output:

```text
y[src, token, hidden]
```

Intent: final output is source-owned. The source rank gathers only the `topk` returned route rows for each token and applies route weights locally.

```python
for src, token_block, hidden_tile:
    acc = 0
    for k in range(topk):
        if valid[src, token, k]:
            v = return_y[src, dst_ord[token,k], entry[token,k], row[token,k], hidden_tile]
            acc += route_weight[token,k] * v
    y[src, token, hidden_tile] = acc
```

### Backward fused stages

`dcombine`

Inputs:

```text
dy[src, token, hidden]
route metadata / inverse queue metadata
route_weight[src, token, k]
```

Outputs:

```text
dy_route[dst, expert, expert_row, hidden]
droute_weight[src, token, k] optionally
```

Intent: route `dy` back from source-token layout to destination expert-major layout. This is the backward analog of combine and is communication-heavy.

```python
for src, token, k, hidden_tile:
    dst, expert, expert_row = inverse_route[src, token, k]
    dy_route[dst, expert, expert_row, hidden_tile] =
        dy[src, token, hidden_tile] * route_weight[src, token, k]
```

`dw2_h`

Inputs:

```text
dy_route[dst, expert, expert_row, hidden]
w2[dst, expert, intermediate, hidden]
```

Output:

```text
dh_expert[dst, expert, expert_row, intermediate]
```

Intent:

```python
dh_expert = dy_route @ w2.T
```

`dw2_w`

Inputs:

```text
h_expert[dst, expert, expert_row, intermediate]
dy_route[dst, expert, expert_row, hidden]
```

Output:

```text
dw2[dst, expert, intermediate, hidden]
```

Intent:

```python
dw2[dst, expert] += h_expert.T @ dy_route
```

`dw13_x`

Inputs:

```text
dz13[dst, expert, expert_row, 2 * intermediate]
w13[dst, expert, hidden, 2 * intermediate]
```

Output:

```text
dx_route[dst, expert, expert_row, hidden]
```

Intent:

```python
dx_route = dz13 @ w13.T
```

`dw13_w`

Inputs:

```text
x_expert[dst, expert, expert_row, hidden]
dz13[dst, expert, expert_row, 2 * intermediate]
```

Output:

```text
dw13[dst, expert, hidden, 2 * intermediate]
```

Intent:

```python
dw13[dst, expert] += x_expert.T @ dz13
```

`dpermute`

Inputs:

```text
dx_route[dst, expert, expert_row, hidden]
inverse route metadata
```

Output:

```text
dx[src, token, hidden]
```

Intent:

```python
for dst, expert, expert_row:
    src, token, k = inverse_route[dst, expert, expert_row]
    dx[src, token, :] += dx_route[dst, expert, expert_row, :]
```

### Semantic work queue model

The clean mental model is a set of semantic work items plus a partial order.

For forward permute/W13:

```text
Permute1(src, dst, entry)
Compute1(dst, src, entry, expert_group, m_tile, n_tile)
```

Partial order:

```text
Permute1(src, dst, entry)
  < Compute1(dst, src, entry, expert_group, m_tile, n_tile)
```

For W2 direct return/combine:

```text
Compute2(dst, expert, row_block, h_tile)
Return2(dst, src, entry, row_block, h_tile)
Combine2(src, token_block, h_tile)
```

Partial order:

```text
Compute2(dst, expert, row_block, h_tile)
  < Return2(dst, src, entry, row_block, h_tile)
  < Combine2(src, token_block, h_tile)
```

The important constraint is that queue entries should be shaped so these work items are block-aligned. If W2 computes a `[M, N]` tile, the return queue should ideally accept that same `[M, N]` tile as one store. If metadata maps arbitrary expert rows to arbitrary queue rows, Mosaic forces illegal or slow per-row scatter. That is why the direct-return path is sensitive to queue discipline.

For backward:

```text
DCombine(src, dst, entry, h_tile)
DW2_H(dst, expert, row_block, i_tile)
DW2_W(dst, expert, i_tile, h_tile)
DW13_X(dst, expert, row_block, hidden_tile)
DW13_W(dst, expert, hidden_tile, intermediate_tile)
DPermute(dst, src, entry, hidden_tile)
```

Partial orders:

```text
DCombine < DW2_H
DCombine < DW2_W
DW2_H   < DW13_X
DW2_H   < DW13_W
DW13_X  < DPermute
```

The same design rule applies: communication queues should expose tiles in the same units that tensorcore kernels consume and produce.

### Direction

Desired final decomposition:

```text
forward:
  fused permute_w13 source-push
  W2 direct return to source queue
  source-owned combine

backward:
  source-owned dcombine / dy route
  W2 backward tensorcore kernels
  W13 backward tensorcore kernels
  source-owned dpermute / dx combine
```

The near-term production question is not “can we write every row somewhere,” but:

```text
Can we define the semantic queues so each fused stage exchanges block-aligned work items?
```

That is the key to avoiding full `recv_x`, dense `partial_y[S,T,H]`, replicated `psum`, per-row remote scatter, and communication/compute serialization.

comments.body:
🤖 Kernel status and current performance summary

Current best integrated semantic fwd+bwd target row:

```text
0.044151736s
175.191 useful TFLOP/s/rank
218.988 rounded TFLOP/s/rank
```

This is much better than the earlier semantic baseline, but still short of the aggregate `250 TFLOP/s/rank` goal. The main remaining tax is not tensorcore math; it is return/combine structure.

| Stage | Current status | Best current timing | Judgment |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `permute_w13` stable source-push inbox | Proven fast path | `216.949 TFLOP/s/rank` median over 48 repeats | Best forward transport+W13 proof. Not the same as current semantic integrated path. |
| semantic `x_pack` / permute scaffold | Correct, production-relevant | `0.006940519s` | Good after H512 tile sweep. |
| semantic `W13` prepacked | Correct | `0.005926196s` | Reasonable, not current bottleneck. |
| source-driven fused W13 | Not promoted | no target success | Lowering blocked on row assembly into WGMMA-compatible SMEM. Stop blind retries. |
| `W2` forward zero-invalid | Correct, good | `0.002586844s` | No longer the obvious bottleneck. |
| forward return/combine owner-sharded | Correct, current best integrated structure | `0.009542040s` isolated | Biggest forward tax. |
| forward direct-return source queue | Under development | no successful timing | Failing before timing; current issue is concrete Mosaic tiled layout for row-offset vector. |
| source-owned gather combine | Correct isolated diagnostic | `0.002740s` combine-only; compare `0.008047s`, diff `0.0` | Semantics are good; direct-return producer not working yet. |
| remote source-gather y return | Correct isolated, rejected integrated | isolated `0.004319881s`; monolithic remote-y `0.047670704s` | Looks good alone, does not compose. |
| `dcombine` / source-expand | Correct | `0.004894563s` | Not the current top bottleneck. |
| W2 backward `dh,dw2` | Correct, strong | `0.005369381s`; isolated `317.9 useful / 397.4 rounded TFLOP/s/rank` | Good tensorcore kernel. |
| W13 backward `dx,dw13` | Correct, strong | `0.009132540s`; mask-elide row `375.9 useful / 469.8 rounded TFLOP/s/rank` | Good, still sizeable because math is large. |
| dx return / dpermute source-gather | Correct | `0.006552185s` | Remaining backward comm tax. |
| dx remote source-gather | Correct, rejected | `0.018706967s`; compare diff `0.0078125` | Too slow. |
| dx copy-only floor | Diagnostic | `0.001364567s` | Shows there is still about a 5ms structural gap. |

Current-best isolated medians:

```text
direct x-pack:                 0.006940519s
W13 prepacked:                 0.005926196s
W2 zero-invalid:               0.002586844s
owner-sharded forward return:  0.009542040s

source-expand / dcombine:      0.004894563s
backward W2:                   0.005369381s
backward W13:                  0.009132540s
dx source-gather return:       0.006552185s
```

Forward-ish isolated sum:

```text
~0.024996s
```

Backward-ish isolated sum:

```text
~0.025949s
```

Naive isolated total:

```text
~0.050945s
```

Actual integrated current-best:

```text
0.044151736s
```

So the integrated graph is not suffering hidden overhead right now; it is faster than the naive sum. The issue is that some individual comm/return stages are still structurally expensive.

Main bottlenecks:

```text
forward return/combine:  ~9.54ms
W13 backward:            ~9.13ms
dx return/dpermute:      ~6.55ms
x-pack/permute:          ~6.94ms
```

The tensorcore-heavy pieces are relatively healthy. The comm-heavy return/combine paths have the biggest gap to their copy-only floors:

```text
forward return copy-only floor: ~1.37ms vs current ~9.54ms
dx return copy-only floor:      ~1.36ms vs current ~6.55ms
```

That is why the next real win is probably queue/ownership structure, not tile tuning.

### Direct-return queue status

The semantic direct-return source queue is the right conceptual direction:

```text
W2 output on destination
-> write bf16 route rows directly into source-owned return_y queue
-> source gathers K route rows per token
```

But it is not yet a working performance path. Recent fixed issues:

```text
missing mesh
bool valid mask 8-byte copy
illegal single-row return store
closed-over row_offsets
iota layout inference
```

Current failure from the latest RNO2A run:

```text
TiledLayout.__init__() missing required tiling parameters
```

So the next fix is to pass a concrete Mosaic tiled layout for the row-offset vector, not bare `mgpu.Layout.TILED`.

Bottom line:

```text
current best: 0.04415s, 175 useful / 219 rounded TFLOP/s/rank
```

The matmul kernels are mostly in decent shape. The remaining performance work should focus on making comm-heavy route return/combine stages exchange block-aligned work items and avoid atomics/dense partial buffers. Direct-return source queue is the active attempt, but it still needs to get through Pallas/Mosaic lowering and then prove correctness/timing.

comments.body:
🤖 JAX semantic source-push milestone and current Hopper ceiling

The research branch now has a package-private semantic MLP custom-VJP boundary with routing metadata built inside JIT, explicit pair/expert capacity clipping, JAX references for every phase, and Pallas implementations for x pack, W13, W2, source-owned return/combine, source-expand, W2/W13 backward, and dX combine. Production matrix multiplies use explicit `mgpu.wgmma`; the semantic plan is slot-free and carries inverse route identity for forward and backward.

Target H100 result: `/dlwh/bench-semantic-mlp-api-dy-replicated-repeat3-20260710-104218`. The manual integrated graph median is `51.465903 ms`, `150.293052` useful TFLOP/s/rank (`187.866314` rounded). The honest custom-VJP API median is `63.038497 ms`, `122.702286` useful TFLOP/s/rank (`153.377857` rounded). All repeats have zero errors, routing drops, metadata overflow, and kernel drops. The `11.572594 ms` / `22.49%` API tax is the all-gather of source-sharded `dy` required by the current destination-pull source-expand.

The current random-routing decomposition is: x pack `10.110 ms`, W13 `6.282 ms`, W2 `2.735 ms`, owner return `9.540 ms`, source-expand `6.479 ms`, W2 backward `5.697 ms`, W13 backward `9.722 ms`, and dX gather `7.214 ms`. Pairwise ideal overlap gives a `~35.85 ms` floor before metadata/all-gather, while 250 useful TFLOP/s/rank requires `~30.94 ms`. Source-push/source-gather expand variants measured `12.18-25.11 ms`, direct remote queues remain numerically wrong, and Mosaic cannot gather arbitrary remote token rows directly into WGMMA-tiled shared memory. This is therefore the measured ceiling of the current split-stage architecture, not an unresolved tile sweep.

Code and the reproducible harness are pushed in PR #6841 at `1a730f23e1`; the PR description now reflects this result.

issues.author: hammer
issues.body:
The [Arcee Trinity Large Technical Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17004) in Section 3.2 Data Preparation defines a metric, Batch Heterogeneity, (BatchHet), that tracks the difference between the maximum microbatch loss and the average loss for each training step, and claim that this metric correlates strongly with gradient norm instability. They note that, as models grow larger, their step-to-step data efficiency tends to increase, and hypothesize that makes them more vulnerable to the step-to-step fluctuations in the data distribution, which causes training instability as models grow larger.

They introduce a method, the Random Sequential Document Buffer (RSDB), to reduce this metric. I'm not sure that method is useful for us as I don't believe we do on-the-fly tokenization. 

Should we track this metric? Given some of the [spikes](https://discord.com/channels/1354881461060243556/1375005693899309126/1479363883813830717) we saw with Delphi that were related to bad data, I have been having bouts of anxiety about some weird data-related training instability hit late in a hero run due to unfortunate sampling packing bad data together in unforeseen ways and have been thinking about how we could mitigate that risk. Adding this metric, creating data that causes it to spike, and developing methods to reduce it even in the face of bad data seems potentially interesting?

issues.author: Helw150
issues.body:
On October 2, new pods failed to start on CoreWeave node `g5bc6da`, blocking new jobs. Kubernetes reported `no space left on device` while creating a pod’s cgroup, the kernel group used to track and limit container resources. The node still reported healthy, and its filesystem had 3.55 TB free.

The host cgroup tree had 65,535 descendant groups. Of these, 65,412 were under `/silo`; that entire subtree contained no processes. This strongly suggests exhaustion of the kernel’s roughly 64K memory-cgroup ID space, though we have not traced the failing allocator.

Silo is the nested container runtime running inside our privileged Iris job `muchanem.cap-pipeline-host-53`. Two sampled container IDs from its `containerd-shim` processes matched empty `/silo` cgroups. This points to a cleanup problem in that workload’s runtime, but we have not identified the code path responsible. We have no evidence that CoreWeave’s host containerd created these groups.

Please investigate whether completed containers leave cgroups and shim processes behind, and fix the cleanup path. Verify that repeated container creation and teardown do not keep increasing either count. Coordinate cleanup of the affected node with the pipeline owner; an empty cgroup alone does not establish that it is safe to remove while the runtime is active.

---

comments.body:
🤖 `g5bc6da` was rebooted to unblock new pods, and the `/silo` cgroup leak started again after the reboot.

**Recovery record (2026-10-02, UTC)**

- The node was cordoned. A drain of the two Iris task pods failed: each pod matched more than one PodDisruptionBudget (Iris keeps one PDB per attempt, for example 7 for `cap-construct-003`), and the eviction API rejects such pods.
- The node was rebooted at approximately 21:45–21:49. The boot ID changed from `ed0d83f7-…` to `c35bfd9c-…`, and the kubelet reported `Ready` at 21:49:15. All pods on the node are new, and new pods start again. The node is uncordoned.
- `muchanem.cap-pipeline-host-53` started again on `g5bc6da` as attempt 79 (pod created 21:45:12).

**Cgroup growth after the reboot**

A read-only debug pod read the host cgroup tree every 30 s:

| UTC | `nr_descendants` | `nr_dying_descendants` | `/silo` children | PIDs under `/silo` | memory `num_cgroups` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 23:05:57 | 347 | 84 | 221 | 54 | 432 |
| 23:07:27 | 355 | 84 | 229 | 59 | 440 |
| 23:09:28 | 360 | 84 | 234 | 101 | 445 |
| 23:10:58 | 365 | 85 | 239 | 90 | 451 |
| 23:13:29 | 374 | 85 | 248 | 126 | 460 |
| 23:14:59 | 386 | 85 | 260 | 112 | 472 |
| 23:16:00 | 398 | 85 | 272 | 120 | 484 |

- All growth is under `/silo`: `nr_descendants` and the `/silo` count increase by the same amount, and the dying count stays at 84–85.
- The number of PIDs under `/silo` goes up and down as containers start and stop, but the `/silo` cgroup count only increases. This agrees with cgroups that stay after their containers stop.
- The rate was about 5 cgroups per minute over the 10 minutes, and about 12 per minute in the last 2 minutes. At 5–12 per minute, the node gets to the limit again in approximately 4–9 days. This projection comes from a 10-minute sample of a variable workload.

**Which count to watch**

- The memory `num_cgroups` value in `/proc/cgroups` is `nr_descendants + nr_dying_descendants + 1` (484 = 398 + 85 + 1 at 23:16). It includes dying cgroups, which still hold a memory-cgroup ID. Thus, it is the value to compare with the limit of approximately 64K IDs.
- `/proc/cgroups` is not namespaced. An unprivileged pod can read the node-wide count with `awk '$1=="memory"{print $3}' /proc/cgroups`. I read 484 from `iris-node-agent` on this node, which agrees with the host value. The pod's own `/sys/fs/cgroup/cgroup.stat` shows only its own subtree (`nr_descendants 0`).

**Other nodes at risk**

25 `muchanem.cap-pipeline-host-*` pods run on 17 nodes in `cw-us-east-02a`. Eight nodes run two each, and many of them have run for 4 days or more: `g73a488`, `g73e352`, `g83d11c`, `ga8db08`, `g845f9c`, `g83d0f6`, `g83c00a`, `g8247ba`. I did not measure their cgroup counts.

comments.author: muchanem
comments.body:
🤖 Silo's sandbox deletion leaked every gVisor (`runsc`) sandbox. All Silo hosts are now stopped and their leaked cgroups removed. Silo stays down until a host with the fix is deployed.

**Cause**

Silo deletes a sandbox with `nerdctl rm -f`. Under `runsc`, nerdctl 2.1.2 kills the sandbox and then tries to delete the task. The delete kills again, `runsc kill` fails with "sandbox is not running", and nerdctl exits 0 anyway. The stopped task, its `containerd-shim`, and its `/silo/<id>` cgroup stay. Silo saw exit 0 and counted the sandbox as deleted.

Reproduced on `cap-pipeline-host-53` (2026-10-04): the same `nerdctl run` then `rm -f` removes everything with `runc`. With `runsc` it exits 0, and the container, its `STOPPED` task, its shim and its empty cgroup remain. The leaked containers carried the label `nerdctl/error: unknown error after kill: runsc did not terminate successfully: exit status 128: sandbox is not running`. Host-53's nested containerd held 19,415 such containers.

**Fix**

`NerdctlRuntime.remove` now checks containerd after `nerdctl rm -f`. If the container is still there, it runs `ctr task delete` (no kill, since the task is already stopped) and then `ctr container delete`. About 0.2% of leaked containers also had `runsc` state that still said "running" for a dead sandbox, and their task delete was refused. For those, `remove` runs `runsc delete --force` first. If the container still cannot be deleted, `remove` raises: the sandbox stays `destroying` and the host's reaper retries it. On host-53, both steps removed the shim and the cgroup. A regression test covers both cases. The fix is on the `mark/silo` branch and is not yet pushed.

**Cleanup (owner-run, 2026-10-04 ~23:05–23:45 UTC)**

All hosts were idle (0 running sandboxes) during the cleanup.

1. On each of the 17 `cap-pipeline-host-*` pods on cw-us-east-02a, I deleted every container with a `STOPPED` task through that host's own containerd, using the sequence above. Live sandbox tasks are `RUNNING`, so they were not touched.
2. I then removed `/silo/<id>` cgroups that were empty, older than 30 minutes, and unknown to that host's containerd.

The node-wide memory `num_cgroups` count fell from 10K–35K to 700–1,250 on 15 nodes. I then cancelled all 17 hosts. The 3 `cap-rno` hosts on cw-rno2a had no leaked containers in their containerd; the sweep removed 10,481 orphaned cgroups on one node and 510 on the other, and those hosts are cancelled too. The `cap-pipeline` broker is still running; it creates no cgroups.

**Not resolved**

- I could not finish two cw-us-east-02a nodes before cancelling. Their empty `/silo` cgroups remain until the cleanup script runs or the node reboots:
  - the node of `cap-pipeline-host-52`, about 33K at the start, where exec stopped responding;
  - the node of `cap-pipeline-host-47`, about 4.3K, where the cleanup was still running.
- About 1–2 containers per host had a zombie sandbox process, and `runsc delete --force` hangs on them. Cancelling the pod clears them. With the fix, `remove` times out after 300 s, logs the failure, and retries on the next reap.
- The cw-rno2a node of `cap-rno-host-4`/`-9` still reports about 12K memory cgroups, but 11,958 of them are dying cgroups (deleted, still pinned by page cache). The kernel frees these as the cache is reclaimed.
- Repeated create and teardown on a deployed host with the fix has not been run yet. It will be checked on the first host brought back, by watching memory `num_cgroups` and the shim count.

issues.author: asartran
issues.body:
The `github.ci` arm of `scripts/ci/wait_for.py` never fires when the installed `gh` lacks `gh pr checks --json`. It reports `0 checks, none failing, not all done` until the overall timeout, even after every check has finished or one has failed. Two PR monitors in the #9812 work lost their CI signal this way: one waited the full 12 hours, the other sat idle for 2h40m.

Reproduce:
1. Use `gh` 2.45.0 (the Ubuntu 24.04 package): `gh pr checks 9860 --repo marin-community/marin --json name,bucket,state` prints `unknown flag: --json` to stderr and nothing to stdout.
2. Run `uv run scripts/ci/wait_for.py --timeout 1h "github.ci 9860"` on a PR whose checks have all finished.

Expected: the arm fires with the CI result, or the command fails with an error saying `gh` is too old.

Cause: `gh_pr_checks` (`scripts/ci/wait_for.py:171`) treats empty stdout as "no checks registered yet" and ignores the exit status and stderr, so the `--json` error looks like a PR with no checks and `evaluate_ci` keeps waiting.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

`github.ci` calls `gh_pr_checks()`, which treats empty stdout as an unregistered check set without inspecting the command exit code. An older `gh` exits nonzero for unsupported `--json`, so the selector repeatedly reports zero checks until timeout.

**Relevant code**
- [`wait_for.py#L170-L189`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/scripts/ci/wait_for.py#L170-L189) — reads check output
- [`wait_for.py#L534-L557`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/scripts/ci/wait_for.py#L534-L557) — evaluates CI state

# Proposed Fix

`CiSource.check()` passes rows from `gh_pr_checks()` to `evaluate_ci()`; the failed `gh` command currently supplies an empty list. Raise `GhError` when stdout is empty and the exit code is nonzero, retaining empty rows for a successful command with no registered checks. Add a regression using a fake older `gh` executable.

comments.body:
🤖

# Research

In [PR #9798](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9798), grader declarations resolve a built `ImageRecipe`, but TaskTrove agent declarations still embed four image digests across executable code, nl2bash, Python tests, and Stack Pytest. Those literals are read directly by converters, so changing an agent image requires manual registry work and cannot follow the recipe build and artifact path. PR #9798 is still open and explicitly leaves automatic agent image preparation for follow-up; I found no overlapping implementation PR.

**Relevant code**
- [`recipes.py#L13-L29`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/378a5e99d6401ce4efbe6465f81f8fd2a1ed4d0f/experiments/post_training/task_curation/images/recipes.py#L13-L29) — grader-only recipe registry
- [`pipeline.py#L115-L165`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/378a5e99d6401ce4efbe6465f81f8fd2a1ed4d0f/experiments/post_training/task_curation/pipeline.py#L115-L165) — literal agent image declaration
- [`pipeline.py#L393-L426`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/378a5e99d6401ce4efbe6465f81f8fd2a1ed4d0f/experiments/post_training/task_curation/pipeline.py#L393-L426) — grader artifact resolution and dependency
- [`inputs.py#L19-L35`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/378a5e99d6401ce4efbe6465f81f8fd2a1ed4d0f/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/pipeline/inputs.py#L19-L35) — conversion context lacks agent environment
- [`python_tests.py#L31-L38`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/378a5e99d6401ce4efbe6465f81f8fd2a1ed4d0f/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/tasktrove/python_tests.py#L31-L38) — two Python image families

# Proposed Fix

Implement this on top of PR #9798 after it merges, or as a stacked PR while it remains open:

1. Add four registered `ImageRecipe`s beside their Dockerfiles: TaskTrove executable code, nl2bash, Python tests, and Stack Pytest. Record pinned bases and locked dependencies in each context. Use the existing `images --recipe <name>` build, push, and artifact path; first inventory the four published images so the new contexts preserve the tools each TaskTrove family needs.
2. Make `RlDataPipeline.environment` hold an `ImageRecipe` or `ShellSim`. In `source_step`, resolve the agent recipe's built digest and add its image artifact as a dependency, just as for `grader_image`. Pass the resolved agent `EnvironmentRequirements` through `SourceRun`, `SourceRecipe`, and `ConversionContext`; converters use `required_agent_environment(context)` when writing `TaskSpec`.
3. Replace the four literal `AgentImage` references in the TaskTrove declarations and converters. Hash the resolved agent digest in `pipeline_identity`, so a recipe change creates a new source artifact. A missing agent artifact should fail with the same explicit build command as a missing grader artifact.
4. Test that every declared agent recipe is registered, converted tasks carry its built digest, changing a recipe renames the source artifact, and `ShellSim` sources remain unaffected. Build and smoke-test each image against a representative TaskTrove task before running sampled controls; verify the pushed digest can be pulled anonymously. Update the image and curation docs with the build commands.

The per-row SWE archive image and grader work named in this issue is a separate follow-up. This plan establishes the recipe mechanism it depends on.

issues.author: rjpower
issues.body:
Follow-up to #9798.

Sources graded by an LLM judge (verifyit checklist and judge modes: tasktrove-codereview, knowledge-openqa, science-openqa, tasktrove-safety, stack_overflow, superuser, tezos, unix, wizard_orca, glaive_code, MultiChallenge) are admitted with an empty verification stage: no control runs because there is no judge client in the grading runtime.

Wanted:

1. A judge test path in `taskcompendium.pipeline.controls`: grade a golden reply (the source's reference output) through the judge and require a passing score, and grade an empty reply and require a failing one, the same way scripted and in-process graders are checked. This needs the runtime judge client (relay endpoint, model revision in the verification identity, cached requests like the review stage).
2. More generally, a "solved environment" check: for any grader kind, take a known-correct submission for a task (reply, workspace files or an oracle command run in the task's agent image) and run it through the task's grader exactly as rollouts would, so every grader has at least one end-to-end positive test before its source is admitted.

The place where the judge control plugs in is marked `TODO(rl-data): judge test path` in the pipeline.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

At the current head of #9798 (`378a5e9`), judge-graded TaskTrove rows are unconditionally `deferred:judge`: the grader requires a model endpoint, while grading machines deny network access. The existing control runner skips a missing golden; empty and negative passes can still make a verification trial pass, and in-process graders bypass source verification on admission. Open-QA tasks carry references, but the checklist-judged sources explicitly have no source gold answer, so a positive witness cannot be inferred for all of them.

**Relevant code**
- [`controls.py#L128-L157`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/378a5e99d6401ce4efbe6465f81f8fd2a1ed4d0f/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/pipeline/controls.py#L128-L157) — skipped golden control
- [`source_verification.py#L301-L311`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/378a5e99d6401ce4efbe6465f81f8fd2a1ed4d0f/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/pipeline/source_verification.py#L301-L311) — skipped golden still permits a pass
- [`source_processing.py#L290-L303`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/378a5e99d6401ce4efbe6465f81f8fd2a1ed4d0f/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/pipeline/source_processing.py#L290-L303) — judge deferral and in-process admission
- [`grade_judge.py#L443-L459`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/378a5e99d6401ce4efbe6465f81f8fd2a1ed4d0f/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_judge.py#L443-L459) — endpoint and model selection
- [`qa.py#L98-L127`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/378a5e99d6401ce4efbe6465f81f8fd2a1ed4d0f/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/tasktrove/qa.py#L98-L127) — open-QA references

# Proposed Fix

1. Add an explicit judge runtime to the trusted grading side of the campaign and rollout path. Resolve relay endpoint, credentials, model, and immutable model revision there; keep credentials out of `TaskSpec` and the agent image. Route judge controls and rollouts through one grading function using verifyit's `JudgeSpec` semantics. Cache validated exact judge requests with the model revision, retain raw responses as evidence, and classify endpoint failures as infrastructure errors. Include the model revision and runtime configuration in `verification_identity` so old trials cannot silently certify a new judge. This needs a shared runtime path because the current sandbox denies network access.
2. Add judge controls for a known-correct reply and an empty reply. Open-QA can use a source reference as the positive candidate. A verbatim reference currently hits verifyit's exact gate, so the judge test must also prove a remote model call succeeds by grading the reference with `exact_gate=False` as a separate probe. Keep the normal end-to-end grade as well. Checklist sources need a real source or authored correct reply; leave them deferred when none exists. Do not treat an invented answer or a skipped golden as positive evidence.
3. Require a passing end-to-end positive control for each grader contract before its source can enter `final/`. Reuse `Reply`, `WorkspaceFiles`, and `OracleCommand` for answer and file tasks; run session graders inside their rollout session. A missing witness leaves the source unverified, a failed witness gates it, and infrastructure failures leave it inconclusive. Remove the in-process admission shortcut and lift unconditional judge deferral only after the judge and positive gates pass.
4. Test the gate with an OpenAI-compatible local judge endpoint and real grading machines: passing golden/failing empty, a wrong golden, missing witness, endpoint failure, model-revision cache invalidation, and a solved workspace or oracle command. Then run a bounded sample campaign and inspect its `verify/` evidence before admitting judge sources.

#9798 is open and owns the grader and pipeline rewrite. Implement this on that branch or after it lands; a parallel PR against the older checkout would duplicate and conflict with that work.

### Slurm wrapper used by every command in this issue

All commands submit `run_gpu.sh` from `$WORK/marin` on the AMD HPC Fund cluster. It turns XLA command buffers off; a later `--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer=...` in `XLA_FLAGS` overrides that. It will be committed to the repo; this comment is the reference until then.

<details><summary>run_gpu.sh</summary>

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -o pipefail
cd "$WORK/marin"
export RAGGED_DOT_IMPL=${RAGGED_DOT_IMPL:-xla} PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
# Command buffers (HIP graphs) corrupt memory on this ROCm stack: nan gradients and segfaults after a few steps.
export XLA_FLAGS="--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer= $XLA_FLAGS"
uv run --no-sync python "$@" 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered -v -E "rocm_pcie_bandwidth|rocm_executor"
```

</details>
